question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026) management said gross margin would bottom at 71-72% in Q4 FY27 due to memory cost inflation, recovering to 72-73% in FY28 when >15% server price increases land. NVIDIA historically issues formal guides close to such verbal previews; GAAP≈non-GAAP (Q2 adjustment only $46M). Anchor midpoint 71.5. Downside risk: memory prices already exceeded expectations and are rising further; upside: earlier price pass-through or Q3 beat. Market check: no human market on Q4 guide; Polymarket only has thin Q3 actual adjusted-GM buckets (73-75% at 0.81, ~2.4k volume) — near-miss contract (Q3 actual, non-GAAP), consistent with Q3 ~74 but not an anchor.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 press release (Aug 26, 2026): Q2 GAAP and non-GAAP GM both 75.0%; Q3 FY27 outlook GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% ±50bp; revenue $108.0B ±2%.
- Q2 FY27 CFO commentary (SEC 8-K): GAAP-to-non-GAAP GM adjustment in Q2 was only $46M acquisition-related costs (<0.1pt); no written Q4 GM guidance in the document.
- Q2 FY27 earnings call (Aug 26, 2026; per multiple outlets incl. gamesreviews, KuCoin blog, Yahoo/BigGo summaries): CFO Kress said GM expected to bottom at 71-72% in Q4 FY27, then recover to 72-73% in FY28 as announced product price increases flow through. Reports framed this as non-GAAP/'gross margins' generally; GAAP has tracked non-GAAP closely.
- Kress described 'extreme pricing conditions in memory', with increases exceeding prior expectations and heading higher into next year; supply commitments more than doubled to $279B; inventory $32B ahead of Vera Rubin ramp.
- NVIDIA told largest customers of >15% server price increases for systems shipping early next year (theresearchnote.com, Aug 2026); article says recovery no earlier than Q4, more plausibly Q1 FY28.
- Vera Rubin production shipments began; billed as fastest ramp ever (new-product ramps historically carry early yield/cost drag).
- Q3 FY27 report expected ~Nov 18, 2026 (MarketBeat); consensus revenue ~$108.8B.
- Status quo: formal Q4 guide lands within management's previewed 71-72% band (midpoint 71.5).
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the midpoint of GAAP gross margin guidance for Q4 FY27 in the 'Outlook' section of the Q3 FY27 press release, rounded to 0.1pt; not non-GAAP, not the call commentary.
- Event window: single publication event, the Q3 FY27 press release (~Nov 18, 2026); as of Oct 21, 2026, pre-release, no update found since the Aug call.
- Markets: no market on the Q4 guide found; only thin Polymarket buckets on Q3 actual adjusted GM.
- Searched for but not found: any October 2026 management update to the Q4 margin view, analyst consensus for the Q4 GM guide, HBM4 contract price specifics.

NVIDIA's next-quarter guides have historically tracked prior-call commentary closely (e.g. 'mid-70s by year end' was followed by a ~75% guide). GAAP now equals non-GAAP, and midpoints tend to be round (x.0/x.5), so 71.0/71.5/72.0 dominate. Downside: memory costs keep rising and Q4 price increases are not yet in effect. Upside: mix/pricing. Memory pricing is 'extreme', above prior expectations, and still rising into next year.
- The SEC CFO commentary (8-K, Aug 2026) has guidance only for Q3, nothing written for Q4. The 71-72% comes from call remarks only.
- Starting Q1 FY27, non-GAAP no longer excludes stock-based comp, so GAAP and non-GAAP GM guides are now identical.
- Earlier guides: Q1 FY27 GAAP GM guide 74.9% +/-50bp (Feb 2026 PR); Q3 FY27 guide 74.0%. Guide midpoints are usually x.0 or x.5 (recent exceptions such as 74.9 came from SBC adjustments that no longer apply).
- Supply commitments rose to $279B from $119B a quarter earlier, mainly memory (Fool/TrendForce, Aug 2026). NVHBM custom HBM was announced.
- Status quo: the guide lands where the CFO's prior commentary pointed (71-72%).
- Directions: lower if memory inflation outruns expectations before price increases take effect (Q1 FY28); higher if mix/pricing or memory relief.
- Resolution: resolves off the GAAP GM midpoint in the 'Outlook' section of the Q3 FY27 press release (expected ~Nov 18-19, 2026), rounded to 0.1%. It does NOT resolve off Q3 actual GM.
- Event window: release date -> single print. As of Oct 21, 2026 the Q3 quarter (ended ~late Oct) is essentially complete; the release is still pending.
- Markets: Polymarket only has Q3 ACTUAL adjusted-GM buckets (low volume). Nothing found for Q4 guidance on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same facts: the 71-72% Q4 bottom from the call, the 74.0% Q3 guide, GAAP=non-GAAP, and no market on the Q4 guide. Run 2's slight upward tilt (71.6) rests on its precedent reading. Run 3's point that SBC is no longer excluded, so the GAAP-vs-non-GAAP gap is gone, removes the main reason for any GAAP-below-non-GAAP discount. No web access this run; I carry forward the shared reference class and a dispersion of ~1.6-1.8. Final median 71.5 with round-number clustering.

disagreements.verdict: Precedents are mixed and memory costs are still rising, so I take 71.5, the signaled midpoint and a round number.
